title: Few-shot Low-resource Knowledge Graph Completion with Multi-view Task Representation Generation

problem.claim: Low-resource knowledge graphs suffer from incompleteness, and missing-triple discovery is hindered by long-tail relations.

gap.claim: Few-shot learning models trained on rich-resource knowledge graphs lack sufficient generalization to address few-shot completion in low-resource knowledge graphs.

contributions.claim: A few-shot learning framework for low-resource knowledge graph completion that uses multi-view task representation generation.
The framework combines a few-shot learner, perturbed few-shot learner, relation knowledge distiller, and pairwise contrastive distiller.
The framework generates multiple views of each few-shot task and distills multi-view relation-representation knowledge into the few-shot learner through a teacher-student setup.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their few-shot learning framework empowered by multi-view task representation generation as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on several real-world low-resource knowledge graphs validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Low-resource knowledge graphs are incomplete, with missing-triple discovery complicated by long-tail relations.
Rich-resource few-shot learning models do not generalize adequately to this low-resource setting.
The paper proposes a multi-view task representation generation framework with four named components.
Different task views are generated and their relation-representation knowledge is distilled into the few-shot learner using pairwise contrastive teacher-student learning.
Experiments on several real-world low-resource knowledge graphs are reported to validate effectiveness.
